To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) inorganic fertilizer is a more important driver of nitrogen pollution than animal manure; (2) denitrification is the primary driver behind the nitrogen pollution; (3) the nitrogen pollution is driven by agricultural land cover and fertilizer application rates; and (4) the nitrogen stable isotope ratios in aquatic food webs are a useful tool for understanding the effects of nitrogen pollution on aquatic ecosystems.

inorganic fertilizer, not manure, is the primary driver for the nitrogen isotopic composition in streams, and that the nitrogen isotopic signal in stream biota is driven primarily by denitrification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of nitrogen stable isotopes in aquatic ecosystems to assess nitrogen pollution.
the effects of anthropogenic sources of nitrogen on the nitrogen stable isotope ratios of aquatic organisms.
the use of stable isotope ratios as tracers of anthropogenic nitrogen inputs to streams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the delta 15N values of aquatic organisms are a good indicator of inorganic N inputs, but not animal manure.
the isotopic signature of the nitrogen in streams in agricultural settings is primarily driven by denitrification of fertilizer inputs, with a minor contribution by denitrification in wetlands.
the nitrogen stable isotope ratios in streams are more strongly influenced by inorganic fertilizers than manures, but that manures can be a significant source of nitrogen in streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inorganic N is more likely than animal N to cause eutrophication, and that denitrification is a more important process than volatilization in determining the fate of N inputs to streams.

the nitrogen isotope ratio of stream water NO3- is a better indicator of the relative importance of inorganic fertilizer and manure than the nitrogen isotope ratios of biota.
